messages:
Sasha: heads up — we're getting a request from a large regulated customer to ship a "metrics bridge" for their private/VPC deployment. requirements: single outbound connection, mTLS, customer KMS envelope, and audit-log hooks into their SIEM. want to align infra + runtime + console UX. who owns the agent shape?

Tom: +1. do we have a preferred pattern? push-from-agent to our ingest, or pull-from-customer sidecar? push seems easier for customers but firewall egress rules are always the pain.

Anjali: most on-prem folks prefer a single outbound to a collector IP/FQDN on 443. minimal ports. we should support both push and pull but start with push-over-mTLS.

Kevin: for auth, customer asked for KMS envelope encryption of payload and a signed JWT for identity. KMS key never leaves customer. we can do envelope: agent encrypts metrics payload -> we decrypt in a customer-managed mirror? need trust boundary design.

Rach: UX: Console should let customers configure (1) bridge mode (push/pull), (2) trusted destination (FQDN/IP), (3) rotate the service cert and link to customer KMS, and (4) toggle audit-log forwarding. prefer a single toggle + permit list for IPs.

Sasha: concrete constraints from security/compliance: no outbound to arbitrary 3rd-party domains, TLS must be mTLS with client cert that can be rotated, and we must surface audit hooks for every exported batch (timestamp, model, route, host, latency, kbatches).

Tom: rough agent config prototype (YAML):
```
agent:
  mode: push
  tls:
    mcert_path: /etc/redwood/agent/cert.pem
    key_path: /etc/redwood/agent/key.pem
  endpoint: https://metrics.bridge.redwood.example:443
  envelope_kms: aws:kms:arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-1234
  batching:
    max_batch_bytes: 512000
    flush_interval_ms: 200
  metrics: [token_rate, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, latency_p50, latency_p95]
```

Anjali: small ask — include `source.id` and `node.role` per envelope so customer's SIEM can map. Also add a `debug` forward mode that sends a compact heartbeat when everything is ok.

Kevin: firewall details — ask customer to open outbound to these IP ranges and FQDN: `metrics.bridge.redwood.example` -> we will provide ASG + region egress list. fallback: proxy via customer's HTTP proxy using CONNECT. Document should include iptables example and proxy env vars.

Sasha: we should avoid requiring customers to open ports other than 443. if customer insists on no direct egress, we can support relay via customer-owned peering or site-to-site but that's heavy. For on-prem air-gapped, we need offline transfer option (S3-compatible endpoint behind a presigned URL) — not first pass.

Rach: dashboard mapping: we need a new “On‑Prem Exports” panel that shows export health, last successful handshake, bytes/sec, batches/dropped, last_kms_decrypt_error. Also flag when agent is running in pull vs push.

Tom: quick note on telemetry shape: prefer protobuf-over-HTTPS with envelope headers. Example envelope header: `X-Export-Version: 1` and `X-Envelope-KID: <kms-key-id>`. Payload is base64(encrypted_protobuf).

Anjali: audit hook: customers want per-batch audit records written to their audit log sink (syslog/HTTPS). We should emit an audit event locally and allow forwarding to configured audit endpoint. Example audit body: `{\"ts\":\"...\",\"batch_id\":\"...\",\"unsealed_size\":12345,\"model\":\"rwd-13b\",\"route\":\"dedicated-west\"}`

Kevin: about KMS — we will support AWS KMS + GCP KMS + customer HSM via PKCS11. For envelope we only need to store `kid` metadata on our side. Actual keys never leave customer. rotate certificate flow: agent should call `POST /v1/agent/renew-csr` and our control plane returns signed cert referencing customer key id.

Sasha: ops question — how will oncall see failures? infra-bot: we can create synthetic metrics `export.connectivity.failed` and `export.kms.decrypt_error` that flow into the normal alerting rules. Also create a dashboard with uptime SLO.

infra-bot: alert rule draft: `sum(increase(export.connectivity.failed[5m])) by (customer) > 0` -> page to infra oncall.

Rach: UX detail — in console when enabling exports, show a pre-flight checklist that lists required firewall rules (e.g., allow outbound 443 to our region IP set or set HTTP_PROXY), required DNS resolution, and example curl handshake for cert verification.

Tom: handshake example (curl):
```
curl --http2 --cert client.pem --key client.key -H \"X-Export-Version:1\" \
  -H \"X-Envelope-KID: arn:aws:kms:...\" \
  -d @payload.bin https://metrics.bridge.redwood.example/ingest
```

Anjali: ops scaling — we need to accept bursts and keep idempotency. include `batch_id` and `seq_num` per batch so retries are safe. also accept small compressed batches (gzip).

Kevin: security review note — we must ensure our relay can't be used as an open proxy. Only accept requests with valid client certs signed by agent CA or with valid signed JWTs we recognize. Also check `source.id` against customer registration.

Sasha: integration items for teams:
- eng-runtime: add envelope + batch headers + batch_id/seq_num support
- eng-platform: console toggle + ipset generation + preflight docs
- infra: provide region egress list + scaling SLOs for bridge endpoints
- eng-security: threat model + cert rotation audit
- support: onboarding playbook and datadog dashboard template

Rach: timelines? can we aim for an internal beta in 3 weeks? minimal: push-over-mTLS, basic envelope header, console toggle, docs.

Tom: 3 weeks seems tight but doable for a limited beta. I'll slice PRs: agent proto change, server ingest changes, docs.

Anjali: I'll draft the preflight doc and firewall checklist and example configs. will include iptables + `HTTP_PROXY` snippet.

Kevin: I'll coordinate KMS/HSM matrix and rotation flow.

Sasha: ok. quick actions: @Tom open a tracking GH issue, @Anjali draft the preflight doc, @Kevin start threat model. we'll sync on Tue infra sync. thanks. :thumbsup:
